articleTitle: Self-Interference Mitigation in In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Using 180° Hybrid Coupler for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In-band full duplex (IBFD) system is an evolving technology in communications, however its implementation is often susceptible to interference. Therefore, this paper proposes to enhance the performance of IBFD system, particularly in the context of fifth-generation (5G) application which is operating within the frequency of 3.5 GHz. By utilizing a Self-Interference Cancellation (SIC) technique, the capability in interference mitigation is investigated by implementing a 180° hybrid coupler on an IBFD antenna integrated with a proximity coupling method. The results show a good performance of refection coefficient on Port $1\left(\mathrm{~S}_{11}\right)$ at the desirable frequency, satisfying predefined standard with the value of less than –10 dB. Moreover, the performance of reflection coefficient on Port $2\left(\mathbf{S}_{22}\right)$ adheres closely to the specified requirement, surpassing the measured value which exceeds $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathrm{dB}$. In addition, the results also highlight the effective isolation which is characterized by polarization tendencies converging towards directional behavior, thus affirming its suitability for 5G application.

articleTitle: A gravity control beam steerable patch antenna utilizing liquid metal flows in fluidic channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: We have designed a double-sided rectangular pattern reconfigurable antenna using liquid metal. The antenna can automatically redirect its main beam direction without any electrical or mechanical control system. With the help of gravity, Gallium-based liquid metal can flow between two channels incorporated into the two sides of the antenna, which in turn changes the main beam direction. This antenna operates at 2.37 GHz and can fix its radiation beam direction when the whole antenna has been rotated by 180 degrees. The realized gain is 6.45 dBi.

articleTitle: UWB Slot Bow-tie Antenna for FMCW GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper describes the design of an ultrawideband (UWB) slot bow-tie antenna, for use in a Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) application. The antenna has a reflection bandwidth from 0.5 GHz to 3 GHz. Two corners of the bow-tie have been blended and the antenna is bent to obtain a unidirectional radiation pattern throughout the frequency range. Isolation of more than 30 dB is achieved between antennas in close proximity.

articleTitle: Design Considerations and Implementation of Coil Detection and Optimized Switching for a Moving Field Inductive Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Powering electric vehicles with on-road charging capabilities eliminates the need for bulky, expensive batteries and enhances their driving range. This addresses a main limitation of current battery-powered electric vehicles. The proposed Moving Field Inductive Power Transfer system, designed for installation on specific highway segments, enables electric vehicles to recharge intermittently while traveling long distances without the need for dedicated charging stops. The primary coils, operating as switched resonant converters embedded in the road, can hand over energy to the next coil, ensuring a continuous power supply follows the vehicle and its onboard secondary coil. This approach significantly reduces power losses in the road-based charging system. This paper outlines the design considerations and showcases an implementation for optimized handover of energy in a scaled model system.

articleTitle: A Multi-band Slot-Coupled Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna Using E-Coupling Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper explores a slot-coupled rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (RDRA) for multi-band functionality. Based on the dielectric waveguide model (DWM), this study estimates resonant frequencies and field patterns of the RDRA modes for modal analysis. By identifying the common characteristic of the required modes, an E-coupling technique is introduced for the mode excitation through adjusting the position of the rectangular slot and open stub length of the microstrip feed line. A series of RDRA modes, including both odd and even modes are simultaneously excited by using this method. A prototype of the RDRA system is fabricated and tested. The reflection coefficients, realized gain, and 3D radiation patterns are measured and reasonable agreement between simulation and measurement results is observed.

articleTitle: Full-wave EM simulation analysis of human body blockage by dense 2D antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Recently, proposals of human-sensing-based services for cellular and local area networks have brought indoor local-ization to the attention of several research groups. In response to these stimuli, various Device-Free Localization (DFL) techniques, also known as Passive Localization methods, have emerged by exploiting ambient signals to locate and track individuals that do not carry any electronic device. This study delves into human passive indoor localization through full-wave electromagnetic simulations. For the scope, we exploit simulations from the commercial tool FEKO® software that employs the Method of Moments (MoM). In particular, we collect and analyze the electric field values in a scenario constituted by a dense 2D/3D deployment of receivers in the presence of an anthropomorphic mobile target. The paper describes in detail the collected dataset and provides a first analysis based on a statistical approach. Possible use cases are also investigated through examples in the context of passive localization, sensing, and imaging.

articleTitle: Development of A Tapered CPW-fed Spline-based Planar Monopole Antenna with Ultra-Wideband Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of a spline-based planar monopole antenna with an ultra-wideband (UWB) characteristics. The proposed antenna consists of a patch section and a groundplane section which are developed by utilizing a quadratic spline formed from a sequence of control points (CPs). The feedline section utilizes a tapered-type of coplanar waveguide (CPW). In order to attain an UWB characteristic, the patch and groundplane sections are configured using 14 and 13 CPs, respectively. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna has UWB characteristics with the working bandwidth from the frequency of 1.76 GHz to more than 20 GHz, with the geometrical bandwidth of $307 \%$. Meanwhile, verification through measurement demonstrates that the realized antenna has the working bandwidth within the frequency range from 2.33 GHz to more than 20 GHz or its geometrical bandwidth of $259 \%$. The measured results of radiation pattern and gain at the frequencies of $4 \mathrm{GHz}, 6 \mathrm{GHz}, 9 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 18 GHz, which are carried out to confirm the simulated results, also show good agreement.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in Surface Wave Fluid Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Background: This paper reports the recent progress in using surface wave fluid antennas to improve multiplex gain and outage probability in mobile communications. Surface wave fluid antennas have been recently proposed to solve fading and interference problems in 5 G mobile communications [1], [2]. Theoretical results showed that noticeable improvements can be obtained. In this paper, a channel model verified by extensive simulation and measured results have been developed for optimizing problems in a downlink Fluid Antenna Multiple Access (FAMA) scenario. The single channel fluid antenna reported in [3] is used, its radiation patterns at 21 fluid radiator positions at 26 GHz have been measured and used in the model.

articleTitle: Bridging Simulation and Measurements through Ray-Launching Analysis: A Study in a Complex Urban Scenario Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: With the rapid increase in mobile subscribers, there is a drive towards achieving higher data rates, prompting the use of higher frequencies in future wireless communication technologies. Wave propagation channel modeling for these frequencies must be considered in conjunction with measurement results. This paper presents a ray-launching (RL)-based simulation in a complex urban scenario characterized by an undulating terrain with a high density of trees. The simulation results tend to closely match the reported measurements when more details are considered. This underscores the benefits of using the RL method, which provides detailed space-time and angle-delay results.

articleTitle: An Initial Study of Human-Scale Blockage in sub-THz Radio Propagation with Application to Indoor Passive Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper empirically investigates the body induced electromagnetic (EM) effects, namely the human body blockage, by conducting indoor measurement campaigns in the unexplored sub-THz W-band $(\mathbf{7 5}-110 \mathrm{GHz})$ and G-band $(170-260 \mathrm{GHz})$. The proposed analysis focuses on both the alterations of channel frequency response induced by body presence, fully or partially obstructing the line-of-sight (LoS) between transmitter and recevier, as well as on the channel impulse response (CIR) for selected movements of the target, i.e. crossing the LoS of the radio link. The proposed study has applications in device-free radio localization and radio frequency (RF) sensing scenarios where the EM radiation or environmental radio signals are collected and processed to detect and locate people without requiring them to wear any electronic devices. Although preliminary, the study reveals that discrimination of the blockage micro-movements is possible, achieving higher precision compared to classical RF sensing and localization using cm-scale wavelengths $\mathbf{(2.4-6 ~ G H z}$ bands).

Author Keywords: channel impulse response integrated sensing and communication

articleTitle: A Clustering Approach for Understanding Bone Health using RF Transmission Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Osteoporosis detection is critical for timely intervention and management of bone health. This paper presents a novel approach utilizing a bow-tie antenna transmit-receive system coupled with classification techniques to detect osteoporosis stages. A cohort of 24 participants, spanning ages 18 to 60 and representing both genders, underwent electromagnetic wave measurements using the Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). The collected data were processed and analyzed using clustering techniques to classify participants into different osteoporosis stages. Results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach in accurately detecting osteoporosis stages, with implications for early diagnosis and personalized treatment.

articleTitle: Circularly-Polarized Compact Antenna Design With OAM Structured Wave Beam Recovery Using Pyramidal Horn Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This article presents a study on the recovery of the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) structured wave produced by a compact fractal antenna designed for vehicular applications in the 5.9 GHz band. The OAM beam carrier field of order -1 was recovered in the far field region by an optimized Pyramidal Horn Reflector (PHR). Simulation results obtained using the CST Studios Suite ${ }^{\text {TM }}$ software showed that, with the application of the PHR reflector, the performance of the parameters the compact receiver fractal antenna, such as the coefficient modulus, impedance, directional gain and polarization were not reduced. Furthermore, phase and amplitude distribution results at 5.9 GHz indicate the presence of the spiral pattern of the OAM beam in the region close to the compact fractal antenna (transmitter) and at the far-field region selected for the receiver.

articleTitle: Comparison of Optimization Techniques and Machine Learning Methods for Optimized Beamforming in Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In today’s wireless networks, particularly in the context of 5G and upcoming 6G networks, parameter optimization using machine learning are crucial. Classical optimization techniques aim to enhance efficiency, while machine learning contributes to predictive capabilities, both critical for the success of next-generation networks. This article explores the utilization of ray tracing to optimize beamforming in wireless communication systems. Specifically, it employs two optimization methods and two classical reinforcement learning approaches to determine the optimal beamforming angles for transmitter and receiver antennas. The goal is to maximize total channel capacity while minimizing interference. By comparing these four methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and execution time, the study aims to identify the most effective approach. This analysis provides information on the strengths and weaknesses of each method, supporting future developments in wireless network optimization.

articleTitle: Propagation and performance analysis of 5G communications in maritime environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The increasing demands for ubiquitous wireless communications has led to multiple new communication scenarios, such as satellite links, maritime networks and Massive Machine-Type Communications. In this work, we investigate the use of 5G New Radio (NR) radio access networks for maritime communication networks. More specifically, this paper aims at evaluating 5G capabilities in maritime environments by investigating the propagation mechanisms that predominate in over-the-sea channels.

articleTitle: Practical Superdirective and Efficient Rectenna for Low-Power RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a superdirective rectenna optimized for enhanced RF-to-DC efficiency and realised gain, featuring direct impedance matching between the antenna and the rectifier. Employing passively loaded, low profile strip dipoles on a low-loss substrate, the rectenna achieves a realised gain of $6.9 \mathrm{d B i}$ and an RF-to-DC efficiency of $22.1 \%$ at $-20 \mathrm{d B m}$.

articleTitle: Integrated antenna design for Autonomous Train Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Traditional train control systems are increasingly evolving around on-board systems, communications, and software, resulting in significant changes that improve control efficiency, reduce headway between trains, and minimize infrastructure and maintenance costs. Currently, widely used communication-based train control (CBTC) systems use two-way radio communication between onboard control systems and ground control systems to significantly reduce train headway, but they have a number of limitations due to their reliance on centralized ground control systems, the limited number of trains they can control, and fixed control flows. To overcome these limitations, the development of autonomous train control systems (ATCS) is underway, which allow trains to determine their own operating authority by increasing cooperation between trains and reducing reliance on ground control commands. For ATCS systems to function effectively, low-latency and highly reliable wireless communications are essential.

articleTitle: AI in Bioelectromagnetics for the Assessment of Safety and Neurorestoration Strategies During Electrical Stimulation Therapies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: To improve our understanding of the effects of electric stimulation, its true safety limits, and potential uses as a therapeutic in the nervous system, we utilize artificial intelligence (AI) in both experimental research and computational modeling. Experimental research is used to identify safety and efficacy trends between electrode designs, stimulation waveforms, and histological changes. Computational modeling research is used to explore potential mechanisms underlying those observed trends. Artificial intelligence is a crucial tool for analysis in both these experimental and modeling tasks.

articleTitle: Compact Robust Antenna Composed of Metal Case with a Slot and Inner Folded Dipole Element
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna composed of metal case with a slot and inner folded dipole antenna. The proposed antenna structure simultaneously achieves the miniaturization of the metal case and the wide bandwidth. The impedance bandwidth of $15.9 \%$ with the size of $0.36 \lambda_{0} \times 0.36 \lambda_{0}$ $\times 0.03 \lambda_{0}$ ($\lambda_{0}$ is the wavelength of low frequency) can be realized by the proposed structure. The proposed structure is validated by the comparison of the simulation and measurement result.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Metaline Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Array antenna techniques have been used for beamforming, where the increase in the gain and communication angle area are realized. The array antenna adopts circularly polarized (CP) antennas are used because the polarization alignment between the transmitting and receiving antennas is not required. In [1], left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) and right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) waves are combined to obtain a linearly polarized wave using hybrid circuits. A CP, small, beam-steerable antenna has been realized using bent metalines [2]. It has a small antenna volume that enables us to make a phased array antenna, achieving either an RHCP or an LHCP wave (single polarization characteristic). So far, the dual polarization characteristic of this phased array antenna has not been discussed. This paper proposes a $4 \times 2$ array antenna for a wireless power transfer (WPT) system, which needs a dual CP wave. This system has the advantage that it does not need hybrid circuits. The proposed antenna is simulated using CST [3].

articleTitle: Enhanced-Bandwidth T-Match Folded Antenna with Advanced Reactance Tunability for Conjugate Impedance Matching with ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This study introduces a T-match Folded Antenna, compares it with a conventional T-match Dipole Antenna, and demonstrates significant enhancements in performance. Both antennas aim for conjugate matching with an IC at 920 MHz on a dielectric substrate with a relative permittivity of 4.3 and a loss tangent of 0.011. The novel folded design achieves an impressive $24.3 \%$ impedance bandwidth from 753 to 977 MHz, significantly outperforming the dipole’s $9.7 \%$ from 870 to 960 MHz. Additionally, the new antenna reduces physical length by 20 mm, optimizing space without using complex structures like meandering. This research highlights the benefits of integrating T-match with folded antennas for improved bandwidth and compactness.

articleTitle: Design of A Metasurface Cavity Antenna for Multiple Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: With the blooming of wireless technology, muti-band high-gain antenna has attracted increasing attention in the past decades. The easiest way to produce a multi-band high-gain antenna is to separately place antenna arrays with different operating bands in the wireless system. However, this leads to a complicated structure and also a low aperture reuse efficiency. In recent years, to improve the aperture reuse efficiency of multi-band high-gain antennas and avoid the requirement of the feeding network, the space-fed shared-aperture antenna which integrates space-fed antennas with different frequency bands together by sharing the same radiating aperture is widely investigated by the researchers, including the hybridization of a Fabry-Perot Cavity antenna (FPCA) with a Fresnel Zone Plate (FZP) lens [1], an FPCA with a folded reflectarray (FRA) [2], and an FPCA with a folded transmitarray (FTA) [3]. Although the above designs successfully demonstrate different techniques in the shared-aperture antenna design, they only realize two operating bands. From the application point of view, more operating bands are preferred in the current wireless communication system to improve the system capacity and spectrum efficiency. Therefore, the investigation of the triple-band shared-aperture antenna is meaningful.

articleTitle: Alternating Generation of Single and Multi-Beam Modes Using the Sequential Rotation Technique in Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A simple technique for generating single and multiple beams from antenna arrays is presented. The approach is based on the sequential rotation technique. It is shown that by applying a controlled second sequential rotation, circularly polarized antenna arrays operating alternately in a single-beam mode M1 and multi-beam mode M2 in the same frequency band can be designed. Proof of the concept is provided in light of case studies. The approach can be applied to large antenna arrays following a modular principle adapted to the array size and needed applications without loss of generality.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coaxial Microstrip Patch Antenna using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents an artificial intelligence-based neurocomputational analysis technique for microstrip patch antennas (MPA) having versatile satellite frequency bands. MPAs are widely researched for their planar design and application in rockets and satellites. Analyzing, designing, and optimizing MPAs is complex due to numerous configuration-dependent geometric parameters, since it is the basic element of a massive array. So, AI-based approaches are increasingly popular among researchers for enhancing MPA analysis, design, and optimization. The proposed antenna has three variable parameters like rectangular radiating patch of width $\left(W_{p}\right)$, length $\left(L_{p}\right)$, and feed location (F). Rest of the parameters like substrate of dielectric coefficient $\epsilon_{r}$, height, and thickness of copper patch are constant.

articleTitle: VoLTE Emergency Call over Assisted-GPS: An Experimental Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This study conducts an experimental evaluation of Assisted GPS (A-GPS) in enhancing Voice over LTE (VoLTE) emergency call systems. Aiming to address the limitations of traditional GPS, such as prolonged Time to First Fix (TTFF), A-GPS leverages additional network data to improve location service efficiency and accuracy. Through the development of specialized source code and the use of laboratory testbeds, the research emulates real-world scenarios to rigorously assess A-GPS’s performance during emergency calls. The investigation focuses on several key performance indicators, including the accuracy of Cell-ID location, satellite detection capabilities, user equipment (UE) response times, horizontal and vertical position errors. Findings reveal that A-GPS markedly enhances location identification, achieving an average horizontal positional error of only 1.49 m and adhering to the 20-second 3 GPP standard for location reporting. These results highlight A-GPS’s significant potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of VoLTE emergency call on mobile devices, offering valuable insights for network operators and emergency services to further refine and optimize emergency communication technologies.

articleTitle: An UWB antenna with total and sharp rejection of WIMAX band using metamaterial cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this letter, an improved applied approach based on hexagonal metamaterial cells for filter-antenna design is presented. It is mainly useful to surmount interferences between users in UWB applications. First, an UWB antenna is designed by using GA, then the undesired WiMAX band (5.7-5.95 GHz) is rejected by optimizing of two pair hexagonal-shaped split ring resonator (SRR) metamaterial cells which are located close to a $50-\Omega$ microstrip feed line. The rejection level of stopband frequencies close to 0 dB and correspond to 5.8 GHz. Extremely interesting simulated results for the reflection coefficient, current distribution and gain are illustrated and discussed.

articleTitle: The Airy Wave Utilization for mm-wave Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The proposal suggests utilizing 1D-Airy waves, generated by manipulating the unit cell of artificial materials at 28 GHz, in a wireless power transfer (WPT) application. These waves possess self-healing, dispersion-less, and self-bending attributes, enhancing their efficiency in carrying energy over long distances compared to conventional dispersion beams. While initially challenging to produce, advancements in artificial material research, specifically in tuning subwavelength-sized unit cells’ phase and amplitude, have facilitated the creation of Airy beam profiles. Previous studies were limited to lower microwave frequencies (1); this study includes analytical analysis at lower mm-wave frequency, i.e., 28 GHz, applicable for mm-wave WPT. This will also reignite interest in the antenna community to design, generate, and use it for WPT applications.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Compact Microstrip Antenna in 2.45 GHz band for Ocean Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Study on marine environment and marine ecosystemic maintenance and study to enable the sustained production of living marine resources have proceeded at authors’ university [1]. As part of these studies, remote monitoring for growth and feed consumption of the fish, and temperature and salinity of the seawater in the offshore fish-tank is required. To achieve the remote monitoring on the ocean, the antenna incorporated inside the buoy (the antenna for Smart buoy) is needed for wireless sensor network in the 2.45 GHz band. It is required that the height and width of the antenna for smart buoy are as small as possible. The omnidirectional pattern with the maximum radiation in the low elevation angle is suitable for ocean wireless sensor network. In [2] [3], the low profile planar antennas with omnidirectional radiation pattern have been proposed for 2.45 GHz band-application. The sizes of these antennas are small. However, the impedance bandwidths are narrow and the gains are small.

articleTitle: Study on Simultaneous Wireless Power Transfer in Air and Underwater Using Magnetic Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in smart aquaculture, which involves activities such as observing tidal currents and fish schools using IoT sensors and drones. This study investigates a method for powering these IoT sensors and drones, both underwater and airborne, using magnetic field-coupled wireless power transmission. Since magnetic fields are generated on both sides of the coil, it is possible to power two terminals simultaneously by placing receiving coils on both sides of a single power supply coil. However, there has been little consideration given to cases where the dielectric constants of the media, such as underwater and airborne environments, differ. In fact, the relative dielectric constant $\varepsilon_{r}$ of water is very high, around 81, compared to the typical dielectric constant $\varepsilon_{r}$ of 2 to 4 for conventional dielectric substrates. As a result, the wavelength becomes much smaller, about 1/10 th of that in air. Therefore, this study conducted a fundamental investigation into a method for simultaneously transmitting wireless power to underwater and airborne environments using a single transmitting coil. First, we examined changes in the magnetic field in the media when the transmitting coil was placed in water, air, and at the boundary surface between water and air. The results revealed that placing the coil on the water surface, i.e., the boundary surface of the media, maximizes the magnetic fields of each medium. Next, we calculated the wireless power transmission efficiency and maximum wireless power transmission efficiency by placing the transmitting coil on the water surface and the receiving coil underwater. The results showed that the maximum wireless power transmission efficiency reaches 80% around the frequency of 2 MHz, compared to the coil resonating around 20 MHz.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of 5G Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, Epsilon-negative (ENG) metasurfaces and their application in enhancing antenna performance for 5G applications are discussed. The detailed design of a unit cell operating at 26GHz is provided and verified via numerical simulations. The proposed unit cell is then implemented to form a metasurface antenna with a circularly polarized radiating patch. By focusing on the S-parameters and permittivity of the ENG metasurface, significant improvements in gain and beamforming capabilities are achieved. Furthermore, enhancements in antenna performance, particularly in terms of efficiency and directive properties, are studied. The analysis reveals that the suggested design empowers the antenna to attain wide-bandwidth capabilities by employing a single metasurface layer. This configuration is distinguished by its low profile and circular polarization, rendering it well-suited for 5G millimeter-wave systems and conducive to MIMO applications.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low-Profile Wideband Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Recently, as wireless communication technology has gradually advanced, the demand for antennas with wideband characteristics continues to increase. Dipole antennas are widely used because they can implement wideband characteristics with a simple structure, and various types of dipole antennas have been presented. Magneto-electric dipole antennas have a directional radiation pattern with a wide bandwidth. Due to these advantages, they are suitable for various wireless communication applications that require broadband and high gain characteristics [1]. However, conventional magneto-electric dipole antennas have a high profile close to $0.25 \lambda_{0}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ is the center frequency of operating bandwidth. Therefore, their application to wireless communication devices is limited. For this reason, various studies have been conducted to reduce the profile of magneto-electric dipole antennas. To reduce the profile of the antenna, the antennas using a bent magnetic dipole were widely used. The antennas using bent magnetic dipoles can achieve a lower profile than antennas with straight magnetic dipoles. However, there are limits to significantly reducing the profile of the antenna.

articleTitle: A Digitally Coded Time-Modulated Transmit Array: Performance Prediction, Optimization and Experimental Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The formulation for the radiated field of a digitally coded time-modulated transmit array is presented. Unlike a conventional time-modulated array, the ON and OFF times in this formulation are in discrete durations within the modulation period. Moreover, both amplitude and phase modulations can be applied simultaneously instead of just amplitude modulation only. Experimental measurements are performed to verify the theoretical predictions of the radiation patterns at the fundamental and harmonic frequencies of the digitally coded time-modulated transmit array.

articleTitle: Dual-Port Folded Dipole Antenna for Harmonic RFID Over Metallic Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-port folded dipole antenna for harmonic radio frequency identification (RFID) over metallic surfaces such as a railway line. The antenna operates at 433 MHz and 866 MHz, which are the two RFID frequencies in Europe. The antenna is designed to be integrated with the metal object itself, using a via to connect the top layer with the ground plane. The antenna is made of FR-4 laminate, a common material for printed circuit boards, which provides good electrical and mechanical performance at a low cost. The antenna design parameters and components are described in detail, along with the simulated results and built prototype. The antenna presents 2.75 and 5.5 dBi of gain for 433 and 866 MHz respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of the Transmission Performance between a Circuit-Shape Slotted Waveguide and a λ/2 dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Scattering parameters (S-parameters) between a prototyped circuit-shape slotted waveguide and a $\lambda / 2$ wavelength dipole antenna were measured and compared with those obtained by the FDTD method. The waveguide was composed of a pair of straight slotted waveguides and a pair of semicircular waveguides, which was proposed and designed for efficient snow melting with microwave radiation to reduce heavy snow removal workloads [1–3].

articleTitle: A BOR-SPR Antenna Operating from 2 GHz to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband BOR-SPR antenna with an antenna height of $0.07 \lambda_{L}\left(\lambda_{L}\right.$: free-space wavelength at 2 GHz) is proposed. It is found that a VSWR of less than 3 is obtained across a frequency range of $2-18 \mathrm{GHz}$ (a fractional bandwidth of $160 \%$). The proposed antenna radiates a conical beam. The antenna gain is more than $-1 \mathbf{d B i}$.

articleTitle: Probe calibration for drone-borne wideband antenna measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Sensor network communications in the HF range came back recently as an alternative to third-party solutions. As an example, over-the-horizon control links in grid energy production facilities can use low-power, low-rate HF transmissions using convolutional coding. Since HF antennas should be characterized in situ, near-field drone-borne measuring systems are convenient. In this paper, we propose to use electrically short, folded dipoles as drone-borne field probes. We present a near-field probe calibration procedure including corrections both for the field-zone and drone body effects.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of 5G Standalone and Non-Standalone Implementations Using Atoll Radio Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Wireless networks are facing rapid evolution, playing increasingly significant roles in global societies and industries. With the emergence of the fifth generation of mobile networks, commonly referred to as 5 G, the connectivity landscape is going through some transformations. This technological advancement aims to promote industrial growth and facilitate innovative applications, with two main architectures emerging: 5 G Standalone (SA) and 5 G Non-Standalone (NSA). NSA builds upon the existing infrastructure of 4 G LTE, while 5 G Standalone represents an autonomous network dedicated to fully realizing the potential of 5G technology.

articleTitle: Coupling Reduction in Two by Two MIMO Vivaldi Antennas For Full Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a two by two Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) Vivaldi antenna has been designed, simulated, fabricated, tested and results compared. The antenna is designed to operate at 3.5 GHz with a bandwidth of $700 \mathrm{MHz}(20 \%)$. The proposed antenna has a gain of approximately 8dB. High isolation up to 70 dB between transmit and receive antennas is achieved by using cross polarization and spatial separation between antennas. Two horizontally polarized (HP) antennas are used for transmitting and two vertically polarized (VP) antennas are used for receiving. The antenna structure is simple and easy to fabricate. The proposed antenna is an excellent candidate for full duplex (FD) and fifth generation (5G) applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Soil Moisture Estimation with Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The measurement of soil water content plays a crucial role in the management of water resources, particularly in agriculture, which consumes over 80% of the managed water supply. An accurate and efficient model for measuring water content can significantly enhance agricultural water usage efficiency, impacting irrigation management, yield prediction, and drought response strategies positively. In this paper, we develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to address the inverse scattering problem by analyzing the complex reflection coefficient to estimate the volumetric water content (VWC) based on electromagnetic properties. The network is trained and tested with a synthetic dataset modeling the multilayered soil. Our results demonstrate the proposed method’s efficiency in estimating soil volumetric water content, showcasing its potential as a tool for improving water resource management in agricultural settings.

articleTitle: A Simulation Study of Specific Absorption Rate With Twisted Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this study, we analyze the radiation properties of the $1 \lambda$-mode loop antenna and identify the superposition of the tangential magnetic field radiated from the two in-phase electric currents as the dominant source of specific absorption rate (SAR). Increasing the physical distance between the currents does not reduce the peak 10 g -SAR levels as the superposition of the magnetic field always generates a single 10 g -SAR hotspot in the middle of the loop. One potential solution to reduce the 10g-SAR for SAR compliance is the excitation of the two current sources with a $\mathbf{1 8 0}$-degree phase difference, this is achieved by introducing a twist in the loop. The twisted loop has two 10 g SAR hotspots with a lower peak level and also achieves a 50% size reduction.

articleTitle: Design of Multiband Large Reflectarray Antennas for Space Applications using Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Modern satellite communications rely on high-gain antennas on board the satellite to establish deep-space communications, provide high-throughput links, or perform high-resolution radiometry. Conventional reflector antennas provide high gain beams, although their large aperture and doubly curved surface make them difficult to manufacture, mount on the satellite, and fold and deploy after the satellite launch.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Omni-Directional Antenna of Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Omnidirectional antennas of circular polarization (CP) are widely used in mobile, vehicular, and satellite communication systems, radio frequency identification (RFID), and radar systems due to their excellent coverage and fading-immune performance under multi-path environments. However, most of the existing omnidirectional CP antennas are of narrow bandwidth. Therefore, it is desirable to design an omnidirectional circularly polarized antenna that can operate over a broad bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Multi-modal Fusion and Mesh-free RCS Prediction Method Based on PointNet++
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Mesh-free method has been a hotspot for calculating electromagnetic scattering characteristics of non-cooperative targets, as the inability of traditional methods to obtain model information of non-cooperative targets and to compute the scattered field by the computational electromagnetic method without meshing. The fitting capabilities of deep learning have quickly gained attention in this area due to their potential to overcome these challenges. This study proposes a novel deep learning framework for predicting the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of PEC objects made of random complex structures under specific conditions. This framework utilizes point cloud and even images as the input, aiming to integrate simulation information such as frequency, angle, and polarization to construct a dataset, and directly predicts the RCS of targets made of PEC material under these specific conditions.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Wideband Antenna on Thin Polyimide Film with Rectangular Slot-Loaded DGS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band, wideband, high-efficiency flexible circular patch antenna for n77, n78, n79, and X band applications. The proposed antenna consists of a circular radiation patch fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) using conductive silver ink mounted on the top surface of the low-profile $50 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ polyimide film. At the substrate’s bottom side, a rectangular slot-loaded defective ground structure (DGS) is added to facilitate $50 \Omega$ impedance matching and enhance the antenna impedance bandwidth. This low-profile antenna design works at two different frequencies, exciting $\mathrm{T M}_{11}$ and higher-order $\mathrm{T M}_{21}$ modes. One operates at 4.4 GHz with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 39.9%, while the other operates at 10 GHz with an FBW of 31.1%. At 4.4 GHz and 10 GHz resonating frequencies, the individual efficiencies are 88% and 91.3%, respectively. This thin film dual-band antenna offers a wide FBW exceeding 20% and a high efficiency of $\gt80 \%$ across both passbands.

articleTitle: PIN-Diode-Based Switchable Polarized Antenna Array with Phase-Shifted Proximity-Coupled-Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of an antenna array utilizing PIN diodes as switches to modify its polarization. The proposed antenna array implements a phase-shifted proximity-coupled feed with a coaxial probe, yielding in a compact configuration. The array is developed on two layers of 1.6 mm thick FR-4 dielectric substrate to operate at the frequency of 3.5 GHz, which falls inside the sub-6 $\mathbf{G H z}$ frequency range employed by 5G technology. In order to produce switchable circular polarization, a circular phase shifted feedline, whose length is equivalent to one wavelength, is applied to excite the four elements of the array. A decoupling mechanism, in the form of an isolation wall, is incorporated to separate physically each element of the array. The characterization results show that the proposed array array can generate switchable circular polarization by biasing the PIN diodes. In addition, to attain the most favorable outcomes, it is imperative to improve the fabrication technique.

articleTitle: Intelligent Automation of Antenna Array Synthesis for RF Safety Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: To keep up with the growing complexity of antennas used for high-speed communication, it is imperative to develop accurate and efficient methods to model such antennas for radio frequency (RF) compliance certification. This paper describes how machine learning optimizations were applied to a ray-tracing implementation of the methodology outlined in the IEC 62232 standard [1] to significantly improve the manual synthesis process.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Vivaldi Antenna for Through-Wall-Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Vivaldi Antenna fed by a microstrip-to-slotline transition for Through-The-Wall Radar Systems Applications. Nowadays, are present a vast number of antennas with Ultra-Wideband (UWB) behavior, although Vivaldi antennas are superior due to their broad bandwidth, high gain, directional radiation pattern and also their capability of being a discrete antenna in terms of size and volume. Through comparative, this paper highlights a Vivaldi antenna with a operating frequency from 1 GHz to 11.4 GHz. This antenna is design on a FR4 substrate with a thickness of approximately 1.3 mm. The proposed antenna shows a stable end-fire radiation from 1 GHz to 9 GHz. The peak gain obtained was of 10.18 dBi and the simulated gain is larger than 4 dBi from 1 GHz to 8 GHz. The Vivaldi antenna present is design and simulated for different parameters in order to study their impact on the antenna performance. The input impedance and the impact of the parameters on the reflection coefficient plots are also shown and analysed.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of 5G and Wi-Fi Private Networks: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: With the advent of Industry 4.0 and the ongoing digital transformation, telecommunications technologies are playing an ever-expanding role in reshaping industrial systems. Within this context, private networks have proven to be a highly attractive solution due to their strong performance in features such as control over network infrastructure, latency, throughput, jitter, reliability, availability, security, scalability and quality of Service (QoS). Considering the technical characteristics of Wi-Fi and 5G technologies, they appear to be potentially suitable solutions to meet these demands.

articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization for Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a study of the impact of miniaturization strategies on radiation efficiency for electrically very small antennas is proposed. Four differential-fed antennas are designed and simulated and then compared at two electrical sizes of ka=0.14 and ka=0.27, with several shapes and with or without a dielectric core material. The excited spherical wave modes of the proposed antennas are $T E_{10}$ and $T M_{10}: T E_{20}$, and the proposed antennas include capacitive loading, material loading, and folding linearly and spirally. It is shown that some miniaturization strategies are more efficient than others, depending on the electrical size of the antenna.

articleTitle: CP Beam-Steerable Metaline Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: A single metaline antenna radiates a beam whose direction is frequency-dependent, i.e., the radiation beam cannot be steered at a fixed operating frequency. This paper resolves the frequency-dependent beam issue by proposing an antenna system composed of multiple metaline antennas. A design process is presented for a circularly polarized (CP) beam that can be steered in the elevation plane at a fixed operating frequency.

articleTitle: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Reinforcement Learning in Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid quantum-classical approach for the optimization of geometrical parameters of a circular patch antenna at 2.4 GHz for wireless applications. The information gathered during electromagnetic (EM) software simulations conducted in the initial design phase is repurposed as training data for constructing a Deep Neural Network (DNN) surrogate model. It serves as a substitute for resource-intensive EM simulations, thereby expediting the training process of reinforcement learning (RL). This acceleration facilitates the optimization process of the electromagnetic design. We also propose to integrate a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) composed of quantum circuits with the classical neural network to create a more expressive model. Moreover, the feasibility of the proposed optimization approach is investigated by comparing its results with those achieved through the traditional Deep Q-Network (DQN) RL algorithm. The experimental results from the hybrid model show its better training convergence while featuring 17 times smaller model complexity compared to regular DQN with only classical neural networks, despite significant time required for model training.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency Decoupling Circuit Integrated with Matching Circuits for a Two-Element Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: With recent improvement in the quality and capacity of wireless communication, multiple antennas techniques, which are used in antenna diversity systems or Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, are becoming important. Also, multi-frequency antennas are required to correspond to communication systems using multi-frequency bands or diversification of wireless systems. There are many reports on the method of decreasing the mutual coupling between two-element antennas in dual-frequency bands. However, in many cases, dual-frequency matching circuits are needed after decreasing the coupling [1], then the circuit loss becomes large.

articleTitle: IPCSBR: A Mesh-Free Intelligence Assisted Point-Cloud Shooting and Bouncing Rays Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Shooting and bouncing rays (SBR) is a classic high frequency asymptotic method (HFAM) in computational electromagnetics (CEM). It is designed to solve electrically large size problems and is widely recognized for both outstanding efficiency and accuracy. SBR has long been used in scattering characteristic analysis, channel modeling and measurements, electromagnetic imaging, and so on. However, despite its prowess, the traditional SBR still has limitations from geometric perspective. For example, most modern SBR simulators only support mesh-based geometry representation. While this may suffice for simple scenes or pre-existing meshes, meshbased SBR encounters efficiency challenges when simulating electromagnetic environments in complex regions like office spaces, modern factories, streets, or during on-site calculations. Thus it is imperative to incorporate more accessible geometry representations into the computational framework of the traditional SBR.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-wave Phased Array Antenna with Subarrays for Indoor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) technology was first introduced by 5G for high-capacity and low-latency communication and phased array antenna modules (PAAMs) are widely used for this purpose [1]. Subarrays are generally applied for enhancing the antenna gain and hence decreasing the power consumption. On one hand, indoor is an important area to be covered by mmWave [2] and the antenna modules used there should have different radiation performance with that for general outdoor applications. Subarrays can be applied for this purpose too. In this paper, we introduce a subarray-based mmWave phased array antenna for indoor applications.

articleTitle: Exploring GNSS Positioning Accuracy for Emergency Calls in Mobile Devices: An Empirical Study using a GNSS Simulator with A-GPS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This research delves into the precision of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning through empirical investigations conducted with a GNSS simulator Spirent GSS7000. The study aims to analyze different factors influencing GNSS [1], particularly for applications like Assisted GPS (A-GPS) [2] used by 4G and 5G networks during emergency calls. Factors such as atmospheric conditions, satellite visibility, signal interference, receiver capabilities, satellite constellation identification and satellite power levels were considered. Using a simulator, it is possible to validate real-world scenarios experienced by mobile devices (UE) during emergency calls. This includes latitude, longitude, altitude, and speed data for locating individuals in emergency scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Band K and Ka Corrugated Horn Antenna for Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: Satellite communication (SatCom) applications cover a wide range of uses, providing connectivity and services in various sectors [1]. Some notable SatCom applications. These applications highlight the diverse and critical roles that satellite communication plays in modern society across various sectors. Advances in satellite technology continue to expand the possibilities and improve the efficiency of these applications [2]. Corrugated Horn Antennas are antennas commonly used in microwave and millimeter-wave frequency bands, and they are essential in several important application areas. Corrugated horn antennas are frequently preferred as feed antennas in parabolic dish antenna systems. This is because these antennas can efficiently illuminate the reflector in a suitable manner, thereby facilitating effective signal transmission and reception [3].

articleTitle: X-Band Antennas for NASA’s Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) Mission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probes (IMAP) is a NASA mission that will launch in 2025. The mission will study the complex dynamics and coupling between the solar wind and the local interstellar medium [1]. The telecommunications system used on the IMAP spacecraft [2] consists of two antennas, pictured in Fig. 1. The antennas are designed to operate over the X-Band frequency assignment for both Near Earth and Deep Space usage, as prescribed by the International Telecommunications Union (ITU). For the Uplink (UL), the frequency ranges from 7145 to 7235 MHz and for the Downlink (DL), from 8400 to 8500 MHz.

articleTitle: Modeling Path Loss in Structured Mango Orchards: An Empirical Approach in Accordance with IEEE 802.11 Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, wirelessly-connected lightweight single-board computers, such as the Raspberry Pi, is employed for measuring path loss (PL) in a structured mango orchards at 2.45 GHz frequency. The experiment involves measuring signal strength (RSSI) at selected Line of Sight (LoS) and Non-Line of Sight (NLOS) points. The present measurement values are obtained during the autumn season, when the trees are in full leaf state and under bright sunny conditions. An empirical model is developed based on these measured values, and then compared with standard vegetation models applicable in IEEE 802.11 standards. Finally, the performance of the proposed model is validated for three cases. The results show good accuracy for the proposed model, with less Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) values compared to the existing models.

articleTitle: Constellation with optimal LEO spacing for satellite-to-mobile downlink communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, we optimize both a very-low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellite mega-constellation and a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellation to achieve a high-rank channel matrix in line-of-sight (LOS) conditions for satellite-to-mobile communications. The optimization of these constellations is achieved through the spacing of the satellites in adjacent planes. The significance of the optimization is that it creates a high-rank channel matrix that delivers the spatial gain in the distributed multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO). The distributed MIMO is modeled as the 4 closest satellites to an unmodified mobile phone, where each satellite is assumed to be a single transmit antenna. For each second the satellites fly over the receiver’s location, a Monte Carlo simulation of the Rician flat fading channel was completed to obtain the mean channel to calculate the capacity. The simulations have shown achievable peak data rates of 177.2 Mbps for the n255 frequency band and 140.9 Mbps for the n256 frequency band at VLEO of 360 km and the LEO we obtained peak data rates of 135.1 Mbps and 102.0 Mbps for the n255 and n256 frequency bands respectively.

articleTitle: A Neural Network Approach for the Solution of an Electromagnetic Inverse Source Problem with SVD-based Pruning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: —In this paper, we face an electromagnetic inverse problem by exploiting Neural Networks (NNs). In particular, we tackle an inverse source problem and propose an iterative pruning scheme based on the use of the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of weight matrices and bias vectors associated to each layer to reduce the NN complexity. The performance of the approach is shown numerically.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Multiband Filtering Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile multi-band filtering patch antenna without any additional filtering circuit is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of three rectangular patches, a pair of differential feeds, and two upper metal strips. By exciting multiple working modes, three working frequency bands, which are $\mathbf{2. 4 - 2. 4 4} \mathrm{GHz}, 3.49-3.53 \mathrm{GHz}$ and $4.86-6.37$ GHz, are realized. The metal strip above and the slot on the patch introduce four radiation nulls, making it a good filtering antenna.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Matrix Compression for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: In this paper a Machine Learning algorithm is used to assist randomized techniques to compress the Method of Moments linear system matrix when analyzing electromagnetic scattering problems modeled with integral equations. Our main focus is the pivot selection procedure, which is a key aspect of the overall compression of the impedance matrix in CUR-like algorithms. We propose the utilization of a random forest model to automatically determine an appropriate dimension for the CUR matrices, thereby ensuring a reasonable compression error without the need of prior information. The random forest methodology seeks to establish links between the key geometric parameters of the electromagnetic interaction under analysis and the optimal number of compression pivots required to achieve the desired compression error. We compare the results obtained using this methodology with those obtained using Adaptive Cross Approximation (ACA), a well-established and reliable compression algorithm widely utilized in practice. Our findings reveal that the CUR with random forest approach achieves faster compression times than ACA, a crucial factor in reducing the computational resources needed for solving scattering problems. Furthermore, the compression error remains adequate and similar in both cases, suggesting the potential benefits of implementing this random forest approach in multilevel algorithms currently employing a CUR-like compression formulation.

articleTitle: Impact of Parallel Interference on FMCW Radar Detection in Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation framework to examine the impact of mutual parallel interference among FMCW radars, considering channel effects like multipath and fading. The simulation employs a comprehensive radar signal processing chain that incorporates realistic antenna patterns, ray tracing, and the analysis of actual hardware configurations, including a Butterworth low-pass filter. Interference arises as radars become increasingly integrated into indoor environments, leading to significant levels of multipath interference. Consequently, radar signals at 60 GHz are modulated to capture safety-critical information about the surrounding environment, including mobile objects such as pedestrians. Propagation parameters are simulated using the electromagnetic field simulator WinProp and further processed within a Python environment with a complete chirp interference model. This simulation workflow yields insights into the radar channel, where real measurements fail due to precise radar synchronization or identical chirp slopes.

articleTitle: Balancing between Data Efficiency and RF-EMF Exposure Reduction Via Beam Switching in 5G mm-Wave Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The rollout of 5G networks is approaching a mature stage globally. This study conducts an exposure assessment in a real-world static indoor environment at 27 GHz. The main goal is to investigate whether beam switching can maintain high data throughput for a user while reducing exposure levels for a non-user. To this aim, we adopt an innovative framework based on a channel sounder able to satisfy the challenging measurements of mm-Wave frequency. This approach allowed us to explore and compare the effectiveness of three different beamforming scenarios. The investigation focuses on diminishing RF-EMF exposure in both line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight situations. The study’s results indicate that it is feasible to use a single beam configuration to meet the required throughput for a targeted user, while also minimizing exposure for another user in a specific location. Additionally, the study contrasts this innovative approach with traditional methods, underscoring the crucial balance between data efficiency and reduced exposure.

articleTitle: Wideband Joint Elevation-Azimuth Angle Estimation Based on Multiple Frequency Model and Atomic Norm Minimizaion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE-APS Topical Conference on Antennas and Propagation in Wireless Communications (APWC)
abstract: The estimation of the Direction of Arrival (DOA) plays a critical role in sonar, radar, and acoustic source localization. However, current research predominantly concentrates on narrowband, one-dimensional signals, which can’t be directly applied to practical scenarios where the signals are usually wideband and multi-dimensional. In this paper, we propose a two-dimensional multi-frequency atomic norm minimization (2DMFANM) algorithm for the estimation of elevation and azimuth angles for wideband signals. A multi-frequency signal representation is adopted to accurately model wideband signals. The technique of atomic norm minimization (ANM) is leveraged to extract DOA information from the received signals in a gridless fashion. To transform the intractable ANM formulation into a solvable semi-definite programming (SDP) problem, we conduct a thorough analysis of the corresponding dual problem. Subsequently, we introduce a novel two-dimensional mapping operator, which aids in the construction of a multivariate trigonometric polynomial representation. This formulation is specifically designed to facilitate the application of the bounded lemma, thereby enabling the transformation of the ANM problem into the SDP framework. Compared with narrowband ANM methods, 2DMFANM takes advantage of additional data from multiple frequencies and remarkably improves the accuracy of estimation. Numerical simulations are executed and demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method than existing algorithms.
